thread:
Sam Huang: Quick heads-up — Ignite POC is hitting high TTFT on small prompts and some cache misses. Users see ~900-1300ms first token, cold starts up to 3s. Also intermittent 429s under burst. Anyone around to swarm?
Andrea Rivera: On it. Which model variant and are they on hosted or dedicated capacity?
Sam Huang: Hosted. Model label in their config: `redwood/gpt-3.5-x-16k@v2-quant`. Requests are tiny single-sentence prompts, concurrency ~6. No explicit batching in client.
Mike Patel: Can you share a couple of sample request IDs or a short snippet of logs where the TTFT is high? Also curious if KV cache warmup is failing.
Sam Huang: Paste of one failed/slow trace (sanitized): ```
[2026-03-20T14:12:01.234Z] req=ak-REDACT id=0x7f3b cpu=0.12s dispatch=0.02s runtime=0.89s first_token=0.92s tokens=1
[2026-03-20T14:12:04.100Z] req=ak-REDACT id=0x7f4c cpu=0.11s dispatch=0.03s runtime=2.8s first_token=2.85s tokens=1
ERROR: cache_miss: prefix_hash=0x9f2a
WARN: batching_disabled: client_concurrency=6
```
Andrea Rivera: Hmm cache_miss lines suggest prefix/KV cache not being used. Are requests coming with identical prompt prefixes? If they vary slightly, cache won't hit.
Sam Huang: They are quite similar — standard product description template with small substitutions (customer_name). We expected prefix caching to help.
Jen O'Neill: Check if they’re sending unique request IDs or random seed headers that invalidate caching. Also confirm they aren't setting `disable_cache` on client side.
Mike Patel: Two quick checks: 1) confirm `x-redwood-hint-prefix` header is present (helps prefix match), 2) look at batching window config — if client sends concurrency but each request has `max_latency_ms` very low, batching might be off.
Sam Huang: I looked — no `x-redwood-hint-prefix` header. Client is JS SDK default. Also the SDK version is 0.9.2 (older).
Andrea Rivera: That explains a lot. Older SDKs didn't send the optimized prefix hints. Recommend upgrading to 1.2.x. Meanwhile we can enable server-side relaxed prefix matching for their org to increase hit rate.
ops-bot: Canary routing updated for org=ignite: relaxed-prefix=true (actor=ops, id=deploy-2917)
Sam Huang: Nice. Any chance the relaxed match will impact quality? They care about exactness.
Mike Patel: Relaxed matching only groups identical start tokens; doesn't rewrite prompts. For their slight substitutions it should help. We'll monitor quality drift in the evals dashboard.
Andrea Rivera: About the 429s — logs show short bursts at 10rps and our hosted per-org throttle at 8rps kicked in. We can provision a short burst allowance for the POC. Sam — can you share expected peak?
Sam Huang: They plan a demo spike to ~15rps for 2 minutes. Can we bump to 20rps for the window?
Jen O'Neill: We can create a temporary quota bump. I'll open a billing approval note for a 24-hour trial bump and document the change.
Sam Huang: Thanks. After the SDK upgrade + relaxed-prefix + quota bump, we'll rerun perf tests tomorrow morning. If TTFT doesn't improve we'll dig deeper into kernel selection and quant path.
Mike Patel: One more thing — add `enable_batching=true` in their client config and set `max_batch_latency_ms` to 25 for demo. That should reduce per-token cost and smooth tail latency.
Sam Huang: Will do. I'll send the SDK upgrade snippet and the batching flag to Ignite now.
Andrea Rivera: I'll monitor logs and post updates here. Tag me if you hit anything weird: @Andrea
Sam Huang: Thanks all :thumbsup:
